messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@payrolliq.com>

Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Prod: sudden tail-latency & 5xx rise — seeing throughput drop

Hi Aditya,

We're seeing a degradation on our end starting ~08:30 PDT today: 99th percentile latency for the /inference route jumped from ~280ms to ~1.6s, and overall throughput has dropped ~30% despite constant incoming QPS. We're also getting intermittent 5xx responses (approx 0.4% of calls) which correlates with spikes in token-generation timeouts.

Quick context: PayrollIQ is on a reserved capacity plan (monthly commit) using the dedicated GPU pool for our production workloads. We've relied on the quiet-period headroom for nightly batch jobs, but today normal daytime traffic appears impacted. We attached a small trace and a CSV export with our client-side timings (stats_snapshot_20260518.csv).

Can you confirm whether you see dedicated pool saturation or reservation drift on Redwood's side? We need an ETA on remediation; payroll processing is time-sensitive and this impacts our SLAs with end customers.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Morales
Director of Platform Engineering, PayrollIQ
elena@payrolliq.com

Subject: RE: Prod: sudden tail-latency & 5xx rise — seeing throughput drop

TL;DR: Reserved pool shows sustained headroom erosion starting 04:00 PDT due to two large scheduled batch jobs (internal customer jobs) overlapping with PayrollIQ's steady traffic. That pushed effective available tokens-per-second below the SLA target; queue growth led to token timeouts and a small rise in 5xx.

What I pulled so far (summary):
- Reservation RDW-9831: 8xA100 nodes reserved. Allocated nodes currently at 8, but the per-node queue depth increased from avg 12 -> 42 between 04:00-09:00 PDT.
- Tail latency (internal telemetry): 99p median of served tokens increased from 280ms -> 1.5s in that window.
- We see a recurring batch job from an internal integration (customer sandbox: sandbox-ingest-job #2741) that kicked off heavy sequence-generation at 03:30 and again at 05:45. The job is mis-tagged as low-priority and did not throttle.
- Autoscaler: no additional dedicated nodes were launched because the autoscaling policy for this customer's pool forbids burst beyond committed GPUs without admin escalation.

Immediate mitigation options (fastest to slowest):
1) Emergency admin override to temporarily allow 20% burst capacity on RDW-9831 (requires exec approval and will bill as additional usage).
2) Apply a temporary rate-limit on non-production routes in the pool (stop sandbox-ingest-job) — fastest and no billing impact.
3) Force route-level fallbacks to smaller model variant for payroll inference calls — requires config change in customer routing (can be done with 10-15 minute push).

I've attached a short log excerpt (PoC_logs_excerpt.txt) showing the queue spikes and a sample token-timeout stack. If we need to involve billing/finance to approve a one-off credit, loop them in.

Next steps proposed:
- Aditya: escalate to ops leadership for burst approval (option 1) OR request the sandbox owner to suspend jobs (option 2).
- Jonas: can you approve a 24-hour emergency burst commit if needed?
- Marissa/Grace: prepare a short customer note to PayrollIQ with mitigation path and expected ETA (30–90 minutes depending on chosen option).

Irene Choi
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com

Attachment: PoC_logs_excerpt.txt

From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Cc: irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>, elena@payrolliq.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: EXEC ESCALATION: Reserved-capacity headroom erosion affecting PayrollIQ (decision + approvals needed)

Jonas/Marissa/Grace — summarizing for exec decision: 

Impact: PayrollIQ production observed 99p latency ~1.5s and throughput drop ~30% between 08:30-09:30 PDT. Customers are reporting degraded UX during payroll runs. This is a reserved-capacity customer (RDW-9831) on a committed plan. 

Cause (current assessment): Overlapping heavy batch jobs (internal sandbox ingest) caused queue growth and effective per-token throughput reduction on reserved nodes. Autoscaler prevented burst due to policy.

Options: 
A) Approve emergency 24-hour burst: +20% GPUs (estimated cost $6.5k) to restore headroom instantly. We bill/credit later or apply a one-off courtesy credit — requires exec sign-off now.
B) Immediate suspension of sandbox workload by engineering (low customer impact) — will restore capacity in 5-10 minutes.
C) Apply route-level fallback to a smaller model variant for PayrollIQ (reduces accuracy slightly) — 10-15 minute config push and no extra cost.

Recommended: Execute B immediately (engineering suspend), follow with C for graceful degradation while we prepare A if the customer requests guaranteed headroom for the rest of the week.

Asks: 
- Jonas: approve option A if customer insists on absolute SLA guarantee across the payroll window. Confirm now/within 20 minutes.
- Marissa/Grace: send the customer note (cc legal/billing as needed) with the mitigation plan and expected ETA (we will offer a one-time 30% invoice credit if we fail to meet the SLA this pay run).
- Irene: after we stabilize, produce a post-incident timeline and remediation plan to prevent non-prod jobs from starving reserved pools (policy + tagging + autoscaler exception process).

I will join the bridge in 5 minutes and will manage the customer comms with Marissa.

— Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer (Escalations Lead), Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
